instructions: For the dipping sauce, stir together 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup water, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp sesame oil, the minced garlic clove and 1 tsp sesame seeds in a small bowl. Set it aside.

In a large bowl, whisk 1 1/2 cups flour, 1 1/2 tbsp potato starch, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp onion powder, 3/4 tsp gochugaru, the 2 eggs and 1 1/2 cups ice-cold water until smooth. The batter should be thin.
Trim the green onions and cut them into 2 to 3 inch pieces. Stir them into the batter until they're coated.

Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add about 1 tbsp oil, then pour in about 1 cup of the batter. Spread it thin so the green onions lie in one layer. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the bottom is crisp and golden.
Flip the pancake and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. Add a little oil around the edge if the pan looks dry. Transfer it to a cutting board.
Repeat with the rest of the batter, using about 1 tbsp of oil for each pancake. If you have a second skillet, run both at once. You should get about 5 pancakes.
Cut the pancakes into squares. Serve with the dipping sauce.
method_notes: Carmyy (5.0 from 31) is the lead: a thin batter of flour, a little potato starch, egg and ice water, with a pile of green onions, fried in plenty of oil and served with a soy, sesame and garlic dipping sauce. The batch is scaled up by half for a lunch for four. The Daring Gourmet (5.0 from 18) and Mission Food agree on cold water, starch for crispness and a thin batter; the sauce is kept to the lead's.
